{{short description|American physical chemist}}
{{More footnotes needed|date=February 2013}}
'''James Andrew McCammon''' (born 1947, [[Lafayette, Indiana]], US) is an American [[physical chemist]] known for his application of principles and methods from theoretical and [[computational chemistry]] to biological systems. He was Distinguished Research Professor of Chemistry and of Pharmacology at the [[University of California, San Diego]], McCammon's research focused on the theoretical aspects of biomolecular and cellular activity. In 2011 he was elected to the [[United States National Academy of Sciences|National Academy of Sciences]].

Prof. McCammon co-authored ''Dynamics of Proteins and Nucleic Acids'' ([[Cambridge University Press]], 1987; {{ISBN|9780521356527}}), an important contribution to [[molecular mechanics]] and [[molecular dynamics]], with [[Stephen Harvey (biologist)|Stephen Harvey]], while the first published reports on molecular mechanics and molecular dynamics can be found as early as 1976, most likely even earlier.

==Early life==
McCammon was born in Lafayette, Indiana and attended [[Pomona College]], graduating in 1969 with a B.A. in chemistry.<ref name="Starr Academy">{{cite news |title=Starr Named to Academy |url=http://magazine.pomona.edu/pomoniana/2020/06/24/starr-named-to-academy/ |accessdate=29 August 2020 |work=Pomona College Magazine |publisher=Pomona College |date=24 June 2020}}</ref> He received his M.A. and Ph.D. from [[Harvard University]]. At Harvard he worked with [[John Deutch]] on the biological applications of [[statistical mechanics]]<ref name="sdsc" /> and theoretical chemist [[Martin Karplus]].<ref>{{cite news |title=Nobel Laureate Martin Karplus ’51 Remembered as Attentive Mentor, ‘Pioneering’ Chemist |url=https://www.thecrimson.com/article/2025/1/10/martin-karplus-obituary/ |access-date=25 October 2026 |work=Harvard Crimson |date=January 10, 2025}}</ref>

==Career==
In the 1980s he helped establish [[computer-aided drug design]] at [[Agouron Pharmaceuticals]] (acquired by Pfizer), contributing to the development of [[nelfinavir]].<ref name="nas" />
He received the Cray Research Information Technology Leadership Award for Breakthrough Computational Science "for his pioneering use of supercomputing technology in analyzing chemical enzyme inhibitors to fight Alzheimers and other diseases."<ref name="sdsc">{{cite web |title=UCSD/SDSC Chemist Receives High Honor in Computational Science |url=https://www.sdsc.edu/news/1995/PR032995.html?image |website=San Diego Supercomputer Center |access-date=25 October 2026 |date=March 28, 1995}}</ref>

== Awards ==
* Elected Member, National Academy of Sciences of the USA (2011)<ref name="nas">{{cite web |title=J. Andrew McCammon - NAS |url=https://www.nasonline.org/directory-entry/j-andrew-mccammon-s3dfux/ |website=National Academy of Sciences |access-date=25 October 2026}}</ref>
* [[American Chemical Society]] (ACS) National Award for ''Computers in Chemical and Pharmaceutical Research'' (2008)
* Elected Fellow, [[American Academy of Arts and Sciences]] (2006)<ref>{{cite web |title=J. Andrew McCammon |url=https://www.amacad.org/person/j-andrew-mccammon |website=American Academy of Arts of Sciences |access-date=25 October 2026}}</ref>
* UCSD SPPS Associated Students Teaching Award (2003)
* UC Chancellor's Associates Award for Research (2002)
* Appointed Investigator, [[Howard Hughes Medical Institute]] (2000–present)
* Joseph E. Mayer Chair of Theoretical Chemistry, UC San Diego (1995-)
* Smithsonian Award for Breakthrough Computational Science (1995)
* Cray Research Information Technology Leadership Award (1995)
* George Hitchings Award for Innovative Methods in Drug Design, Burroughs Wellcome Fund (1987–1992)
* Dreyfus Teacher-Scholar Award (1982–87)
* NIH Research Career Development Award (1980–85)
